p0.title: Plan re-merge silently discards replacementProgress, re-issuing chunk 1 (duplicate intents)
p0.evidence: The f5b0t contract states only that the legacy scalar is preserved; it never says replacementProgress must survive a plan rewrite. The single plan writer rebuilds every entry from scratch carrying exactly one prior field — examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2877-2884 `replacementSequence: prior?.replacementSequence ?? null` — and its no-op short-circuit comparator ignores any new member (index.ts:2835-2839 `sameSettlementEntry`, used by the `unchanged` test at :2893-2901). The accepted design mandates this merge on every restart *before any issue* and requires the entry set to change (.logs/d110c-0c1f5b0r-design-3a156aca/design.md step 3: "a replacement row that is itself displaced becomes a new source entry", "An entry whose source row now classifies terminal ... is removed from the plan at merge", "Write it with transactWriteSettlementPlan (CAS on revision) before any issue"). Any such rewrite while a consumed prefix is partial resets the entry to unlinked-with-no-progress, and the drain at index.ts:2973-2974 then re-derives the full ordered list and re-issues intents 1..p a second time. This is the exact duplicate-intent failure RED item 5 claims to exclude.
p0.correction: Add one invariant to the contract: an entry carried forward by a plan merge/rewrite MUST carry its `replacementProgress` byte-for-byte, the merge comparator MUST include it, and `transactWriteSettlementPlan` MUST refuse a write that drops or shrinks an existing entry's chunk prefix for an unchanged (sourceSequence, sourceDigest, disposition) triple.

p0.title: Store-side prefix/digest refusal is post-signature and permanently halts operation admission, so "reread the plan and continue" is unreachable
p0.evidence: The contract makes stale-prefix/wrong-digest refusals a routine outcome (`ISSUANCE_RETRY_REQUIRED` for "a structurally valid but stale plan comparison"; the room "rereads the plan, and continues"). But the plan effect is applied inside `transactIssue` after `buildAndSign` has already signed (packages/issuance-store/src/conformance.ts:315 then :327-335; `applySettlementPlanEffect` at packages/issuance-store/src/contract.ts:429-433 throws `ISSUANCE_RETRY_REQUIRED`). That throw lands in packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6468-6490 with `signerResolved === true` and `reservation` non-undefined (replacements are application operations, so `controlOperation` is false at :6346/:6354 and `reserveOperation` returns a value), which takes the branch at :6473-6474 and sets `registration.operationAdmissionHalted = true`. That flag is terminal — `issueOneVertex` refuses everything afterwards at :6329 and it is only ever cleared at registration creation (:8363) — and the room sees `admission-rejected`, not a retryable outcome. So a benign CAS/stale-prefix refusal bricks the plane mid-settlement instead of allowing resume, and "refuses before mutation" is true only of durable state, not of the plane.
p0.correction: Require the Node issue owner to read the plan and validate digest, `fromIntent` vs durable prefix, and range *before* `buildAndSign`, returning a distinct nonmutating `V3LocalIssueResult` kind that does not set `operationAdmissionHalted`; keep the in-transaction store check as the authoritative re-check and state explicitly that its failure is a reopen-required outcome, not a plane halt.

p1.title: intentCount/intentDigest origination is unspecified; lazy creation reproduces the false-completion bug the slice exists to fix
p1.evidence: The progress record carries `version`, `intentCount`, `intentDigest`, `chunks`, but the additive effect fields are only `sourceSequence`, `intentDigest`, `fromIntent`, `throughIntent` — no `intentCount`. The contract says the store "atomically appends the chunk" and that the scalar fills "only when the prefix reaches intentCount", but never says who first writes `intentCount`/`intentDigest`, nor what happens to a progress effect against an entry that has no `replacementProgress`. The only hint is the migration bullet ("may be CAS-upgraded to the progress form ... before replacement issue"). If a backend instead creates the record lazily on the first chunk it must infer `intentCount`, and inferring it from `throughIntent` marks a 2-chunk replacement complete after chunk 1 — verbatim the defect quoted in the slice's own Status paragraph.
p1.correction: State that the room establishes `replacementProgress` (version 1, intentCount, intentDigest, zero chunks) through `transactWriteSettlementPlan` CAS before the first replacement issue, and that a progress effect against an entry without a durable `replacementProgress`, or with a mismatching `intentDigest`, is refused with no mutation.

p1.title: Repointing APPLICATION_BATCH_MAX_ENTRIES at the issuance-store bound moves a peer-vertex admission threshold into the issuance package
p1.evidence: The contract directs `SETTLEMENT_REPLACEMENT_MAX_INTENTS` to be used for "Node's existing application-batch entry ceiling so the two cannot drift". That ceiling is packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:235, consumed at :6169 inside `applicationBatchEntries`, which is reached from `acceptedApplicationOperation` (:6200-6208) on the authenticated-ingress paths at :3984, :5586, :5734, :5762, :5789 — i.e. it decides acceptance of batch vertices authored by *other* peers, and it also gates the frozen 64-writer workload. Repointing it makes a network-facing admission threshold owned by `@ts-drp/issuance-store`, contradicting this slice's own "No ... threshold ... change is authorized" and "the durable/public issuance-store type addition is the entire compatibility cost". The value is 16 in both places today, so nothing changes now; the defect is the ownership/drift channel pointing the wrong way.
p1.correction: Leave `APPLICATION_BATCH_MAX_ENTRIES` as Node's owned acceptance constant and enforce anti-drift with a typecheck/test equality assertion against `SETTLEMENT_REPLACEMENT_MAX_INTENTS` instead of substituting the import.

p1.title: No Node failure kind is assigned to the new refusals, so the room cannot separate retryable from fail-closed
p1.evidence: The error-ownership paragraph names only issuance-store codes (`ISSUANCE_RECOVERY_CORRUPT`, `ISSUANCE_COMMIT_INVALID`, `ISSUANCE_RETRY_REQUIRED`), but every refusal reaches the room as a `V3LocalIssueResult` kind from the closed set at packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:540-551. The 5-key effect is currently rejected as `malformed-input` at :6244-6258, and post-transaction failures collapse to `admission-rejected`/`issuance-rejected` at :6486-6490. The room branches only on `!issued.ok` (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2934-2941), so a stale-prefix refusal the contract wants retried and a digest mismatch the contract requires to fail closed ("mismatch fails closed and does not issue, relink, rebuild or downgrade") are indistinguishable.
p1.correction: Pin the exact `V3LocalIssueResult` kind for each new refusal class (shape/range, digest mismatch, stale prefix) and state which one the room retries after a plan reread versus halts on.

p1.title: Partial progress is not reconciled with the design's merge-time entry removal and displaced-replacement re-sourcing
p1.evidence: design.md step 3 removes an entry whose source row now classifies terminal, and turns a displaced replacement row into a new source entry. The f5b0t contract only says "The room resumes at the durable consumed prefix" and never states what happens when an entry with a nonzero prefix is removed at merge (intents p+1..n are dropped — a skipped intent), or when the vertex carrying chunk 1 is itself displaced and re-sourced while the original entry still resumes at p+1 (intents 1..p are re-derived under the new entry while the old entry skips them). RED item 5 asserts "no skipped, duplicated or substituted intent" across close/reopen, so the RED will hit both cases with no specified expected behavior.
p1.correction: State the two rules explicitly: an entry with a nonzero consumed prefix may not be removed at merge (or, if removal is intended, that the remaining suffix is deliberately abandoned and why), and a displaced partial-chunk row that becomes a new source entry does not rewind the original entry's prefix.

p1.title: logicalTime monotonicity across the chunks of one replacement is unpinned and the counter is not durable
p1.evidence: Splitting one replacement vertex into several newly exposes its operation run to a counter reset. `logicalTime` is in-memory, seeded from `input.initialLogicalTime` (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:1811), raised only by observed vertices (:1913-1922), and allocated per replacement operation at :3006-3007. Node enforces strict increase only *within* one submission (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6269-6276, :6306), not across vertices. After a crash between chunk 1 and chunk 2 the reopened room can allocate chunk 2 logical times at or below chunk 1's, reordering the same source's intents — and the contract deliberately excludes logicalTime from the binding digest, so nothing detects it.
p1.correction: Require the room to seed the replacement run from a durable floor (e.g. strictly above the logicalTime of the last recorded chunk) and state that chunk k+1's first logicalTime must exceed chunk k's last, or state explicitly why intra-source logicalTime order is irrelevant to the application.

p2.title: Canonical limits for the binding digest encode are unspecified and differ from Node's issue-time limits
p2.evidence: The expression is `hashDomain("ts-drp/settlement-replacement-intents/v1", encodeCanonical(orderedReplacementOperations))` with no limits argument, so it uses DEFAULT_LIMITS (maxDepth 128, maxItems 1e6, maxBytes 256 MiB — packages/canonical/src/index.ts:27-31), whereas Node encodes and accepts the same operations under APPLICATION_BATCH_LIMITS (65,536 bytes, depth 8, 1,024 items — packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:236, :6222-6229). A list that digests cleanly can therefore be one Node will never accept, and the contract forbids any downgrade out of that state ("Reject ... converting a valid multi-intent replacement to manual review or unsupported status").
p2.disposition: Name the exact limits profile used for the digest encode and require the room to reject the list before pinning progress if any operation fails to encode under Node's batch limits.

p2.title: intentCount is not defined against the expire filter
p2.evidence: The room's replacement list is `source.intents` with `policy === "expire"` entries dropped (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2977-3009), so it can be shorter than `source.intents.length` and shorter than the `operationCount` each intent carries (:2826-2827, set by `rebaseIntents` at packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6839-6841). The contract says only "intentCount in 1..16".
p2.disposition: State that intentCount is the length of the post-policy ordered replacement-operation list, not the source intent or operationCount.

p2.title: A new hash domain is introduced under a "no cryptography change" scope sentence
p2.evidence: The contract adds the domain "ts-drp/settlement-replacement-intents/v1" while asserting "No wire envelope, protobuf, checkpoint, anchor, authority, cryptography, dependency, threshold, workload or public Node issue-input change is authorized". `hashDomain` is documented as taking a "Registered hash domain" (packages/canonical/src/index.ts:556-561) and the plan document is the de-facto registry. The value is device-local and never on the wire, so this is a wording/registration gap rather than a protocol change.
p2.disposition: Register the new domain alongside the existing v3 domains in the plan and reword the scope sentence to "no wire-bound cryptographic domain or suite change".

p2.title: "transform growth" wording conflicts with the derivation that makes 16 correct
p2.evidence: 16 is correct: `rebaseIntents` yields at most APPLICATION_BATCH_MAX_ENTRIES intents for a batch source (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6169, :6838-6841) or exactly 1 otherwise, and the room's transform is a stability-checked 1→1 map (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2989-3005), so the ordered list can never exceed 16. RED item 4's phrase "transform growth" can be read as intent-count growth, which would invalidate the bound.
p2.disposition: Reword to "transform byte growth" and record that the 1→1 transform contract is what makes 1..16 exhaustive.

p2.title: The bound and the new symbols must be proven behaviorally, not by importing them
p2.evidence: RED acceptance requires "failure is behavioral and not a missing import/export", but item 1 asks to prove "the bound" and the new shapes, and `SETTLEMENT_REPLACEMENT_MAX_INTENTS`, `SettlementReplacementProgress` and the optional entry member do not exist yet. A test that imports the constant or annotates a fixture with the new type fails at resolution/typecheck. Behavioral probes do exist: an untyped 5-key entry fixture through `copySettlementPlan` returns undefined today (packages/issuance-store/src/contract.ts:299-319), a 5-key effect throws ISSUANCE_COMMIT_INVALID (:285-297 via :470-491), and a 17-operation `issueLocal` splits at 16 (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6701-6711).
p2.disposition: Require all new-shape and bound assertions to run through `unknown` fixtures and existing exported validators, and to assert Node's ceiling via observed split behavior rather than by importing the constant.

structured_output.summary: The slice's premise is accurate and verified: the entry holds one scalar (types.ts:50-55), `applySettlementPlanEffect` can fill it exactly once (contract.ts:429-433), the room submits all replacement intents in one call (index.ts:3011-3014), and Node returns `split-required` nonmutatingly before issuing (v3-live.ts:6701-6711). The bound is right — `rebaseIntents` yields at most 16 intents and the room's transform is a stability-checked 1→1 map, so 1..16 is exhaustive and cannot be exceeded by rebase or transform. Legacy compatibility is largely sound: exact-key entry validation makes an old reader fail closed and poison rather than downgrade (node-issuance-store.ts:387-416, :584-595), browser DATABASE_VERSION stays 2 with the same four stores, `hashDomain` is already available to the room, and `@ts-drp/node` already depends on `@ts-drp/issuance-store`, so no new dependency is implied. Two blockers remain. First, the contract's only stated preservation rule is the scalar, while the design mandates a plan re-merge before every issue and the sole plan writer rebuilds entries carrying just `replacementSequence` — so any rewrite during a partial prefix erases progress and re-issues chunk 1, the exact duplicate the slice exists to prevent. Second, prefix/digest refusals land inside `transactIssue` after signing, and Node's catch sets the terminal `operationAdmissionHalted` flag, so the specified "reread the plan and continue" resume is unreachable and a routine stale-prefix retry bricks the plane. Five P1s cover unspecified `intentCount` origination (whose lazy-creation reading reproduces the false-completion bug verbatim), the admission-threshold ownership move, unassigned Node failure kinds, the unreconciled merge-removal/re-sourcing cases, and unpinned cross-chunk logicalTime. With those corrections the contract is exact enough for tests-only RED; as written the RED matrix would have to invent the missing rules.
